relevance.rationale: Directly on QOU's subject matter (q-deformed polylogarithms) but with a DIFFERENT deformation: Schlesinger uses Li_{n_1..n_m}(z;q) = sum z^k/(1-q^k)^n, and says explicitly that this differs from the Kirillov/Koornwinder deformations usually discussed. QOU's Li_2^q is sum x^n/(n [n]_q). So nothing here transfers to QOU's object without a conversion that the paper does not supply, and I have not checked whether one exists. What is usable is structural: Schlesinger's whole point is that HIS choice of deformation is the one that makes the q-polylogarithms close under multiplication (Lemma 2) and preserve the classical shuffle/symmetry and distribution relations (Cor. 3, Lemma 4). That is a sharp question to ask of QOU's Li_2^q, which the corpus tags 'hopf-algebra' at rem:q-dilog-three-contexts without establishing any algebra structure.

keyResults.statement: The rational span of the q-deformed multiple polylogarithms Li_{n_1..n_m}(z_1..z_m;q) is an associative Q-algebra, and the classical symmetry (shuffle) relation Li_1(x,q)Li_1(y,q) = Li_{1,1}(x,y,q) + Li_{1,1}(y,x,q) + Li_2(xy,q) survives the deformation.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the precise test QOU's own Li_2^q must pass for the 'hopf-algebra' tag on rem:q-dilog-three-contexts to be earned, and a worked example of a deformation for which it does pass. Consumable as a remark stating that algebra-closure is deformation-dependent and is not automatic for QOU's normalisation.

keyResults.statement: q-deformed distribution relation: Li_2(x, q^n) = (1/n) sum_{y^n = x} Li_2(y, q), and similarly for Li_{1,1}.
keyResults.useForFolio: The q-analogue of exactly the classical distribution/multiplication identity sum_k Li_3(zeta_N^k) = (N^{1-3} - 1) zeta(3) that prop:cl3-zeta5-orbit-sum-identity and conj:bring-trilog-depth-3-witness rest on. Worth a compute-check: does the orbit-sum identity QOU uses survive in QOU's own q-normalisation, or only in Schlesinger's? A negative answer would be informative about the pre-/post-archimedean 'accident' classification in rem:transcendental-accounting.

proposedActions.rationale: Test whether the orbit-sum / distribution identity used by prop:cl3-zeta5-orbit-sum-identity holds for QOU's Li_2^q = sum x^n/(n [n]_q), as Lemma 4 shows it does for Schlesinger's normalisation. This is a falsifiable numeric check, not an adoption of his result.

Record that algebra-closure and shuffle-preservation of q-polylogarithms are normalisation-dependent, and that rem:q-dilog-three-contexts' 'hopf-algebra' tag is currently unbacked for QOU's own normalisation.
